title: Timezone picker is inert: all 18 options are IANA names, and the clock parser accepts none of them
summary: Half of this was already closed by an earlier wave and half of what that wave did was an INVERSION that made the app record and schedule against a time that never happened. Already closed (verified in the tree, not assumed): the picker no longer offers unparseable IANA names - packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/location_settings.dart:846 kUtcOffsetTimezones is 38 UTC offsets, kLegacyIanaUtcOffsets + _migrateLegacyTimezone rewrite a stored IANA label onto its standard-time offset, and the surfaces the verifier named now read clockProvider (status bar temperature_and_time.dart:161, dashboard_header_actions.dart:105, night_timeline.dart:42, moon_card.dart:38, command_bar.dart:568). What was NOT closed, and is what I fixed: Clock.now() is a RENDERING, not an instant - FixedOffsetClock shifts the field values and hands them back tagged isUtc:false, so now().toUtc() / .millisecondsSinceEpoch / difference against a real timestamp all land chosenOffset + hostOffset away (measured: 13h for a +09:00 site on a -04:00 host). Making the picker resolve therefore armed that footgun at five production call sites that need an instant: the FITS DATE-OBS / captured_images fallback timestamp, the stale-frame reference for a timed-out exposure, the keeper-numbering filename probe, the temp-capture filename, and the whole scheduler. The scheduler was doubly wrong - SchedulerSite.localOffset was DateTime.now().timeZoneOffset, the LAPTOP's offset, so 'image between 22:00 and 04:00 local' was judged in the operator's zone and never reached the observatory's, which is verbatim the finding's own 'host-local scheduler decisions while the UI shows the timezone they chose'. Fix: Clock gains nowUtc() (the true instant) and utcOffset (the chosen zone), every instant consumer moved to them, the scheduler site offset now comes from the clock and follows a Timezone edit via a new ref.listen(clockProvider). Also finished the display side the earlier wave stopped short of: the Dashboard Tonight card's 'Twilight HH:MM' and the cockpit sky panel's idle 'astro dark HH:MM -> HH:MM' were still host-local, so one screen showed two zones with nothing saying which was which.
files_changed: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/clock_provider.dart (Clock gains nowUtc() + utcOffset; SystemClock and FixedOffsetClock implement both; now()'s doc says plainly that it is a rendering and must never be rebased)
packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service.dart (3 sites: exposureStartedAt staleness reference, the unparseable-bridge-timestamp DATE-OBS fallback, the temp-capture filename epoch millis)
packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/imaging_service/file_paths.dart (keeper-numbering probe timestamp: now().toUtc() -> nowUtc(), so the probe and the real save render the same $DATE/$DATETIME)

packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/scheduler_provider.dart (FOUR sites: SchedulerSite.localOffset in the engine constructor AND in schedulerEngineReadyProvider's post-construction hydrate - the second one was re-applying the host offset on every cold start and would have silently undone the first; engine clock: clock.now -> clock.nowUtc; previewDecision/previewRanking likewise; NEW ref.listen(clockProvider) so a Timezone edit moves a live engine - the settings listener could not do it because clockProvider is not flushed yet at that point)

cd packages/skotiq_core && flutter test (whole package) -> 5477 passing, 4 skipped, 6 failing, ALL 6 pre-existing in test/services/import/nina_sequence_fidelity_test.dart with 'SequenceImportValidationFailedException: 1 blocking issue(s) [Wait Has No Time Set]' - sequence-import validation, no clock/scheduler/imaging involvement, and neither the importer nor its test is touched by this change

cd packages/skotiq_app && flutter test (whole package) -> 2851 passing, 47 failing. 45 are golden/screenshot pixel comparisons failing at 40%+ whole-frame diff across 15 screens I never touched (weather, guiding, onboarding, settings, equipment, polar alignment ...) - the documented Windows-captured-goldens-on-Linux baseline. The other 2 (first_light_retry_requery_test, search_command_focus_test) PASS when run on their own, so they are parallel-shard flakes, not regressions.

revert_check:
Four severs, each at the production call site, each restored and re-verified green.
(1) imaging_service.dart:461 `captureTimestamp = _ref.read(clockProvider).nowUtc();` -> `.now();`  ->  imaging_capture_timestamp_timezone_test 'a zone override does not move the recorded observation time' FAILED: 'the frame is recorded as taken in the future - the chosen zone leaked into an instant'. This drives the real ImagingService.captureImage against a MockBackend whose camera returns an unparseable timestamp, and reads capturedAt off the returned CapturedImageData - the value that becomes FITS DATE-OBS and the captured_images row.
(2) scheduler_provider.dart:704 `final localOffset = clock.utcOffset;` -> `DateTime.now().timeZoneOffset;`  ->  'site offset comes from the Timezone setting' FAILED: Expected Duration:<5:45:00> Actual Duration:<-4:00:00> (the host's), and 'changing the Timezone setting moves the running engine' FAILED too.
(3) scheduler_provider.dart:733 `clock: clock.nowUtc,` -> `clock: clock.now,`  ->  'evaluation timestamps the real instant, not the rendering' FAILED: Expected less than 0:01:00, Actual 9:44:59.700460 - exactly the chosen 5h45m plus the host's 4h. Read off SchedulerDecision.evaluatedAt, which is the engine's injected clock verbatim, after driving engine.requestReevaluation() on the real schedulerEngineProvider.
(4) tonight_card.dart:103 `astroTwilightTime = hhmm(dusk);` -> the raw `dusk.hour/dusk.minute` string, AND cockpit_sky_context.dart:180 back to `formatTimeOfDay(dusk)`  ->  both dashboard_twilight_timezone_test zone cases FAILED: 'Found 0 widgets with text "20:22"' and 'Found 0 widgets with text "No target - astro dark 20:22:00->05:50:00 ..."'. Pumped through the real provider graph (app_settings -> clockProvider -> widget), not a helper call.
(5) scheduler_provider.dart:826 (schedulerEngineReadyProvider) `localOffset: ref.read(clockProvider).utcOffset` -> `DateTime.now().timeZoneOffset`  ->  'the ready gate does not put the host offset back' FAILED: Expected Duration:<5:45:00> Actual Duration:<-4:00:00>. This site was found only by sweeping every SchedulerSite construction after fixing the first one; it hydrates the site AFTER the constructor and would have silently undone sever (2)'s fix on every cold start.
Also severed by construction: removing the new ref.listen(clockProvider) in scheduler_provider is what the 'changing the Timezone setting moves the running engine' test was written against - it failed (Expected -9:30:00, Actual 5:45:00) before that listener existed, which is how the Riverpod flush-ordering trap was found in the first place.
caveats: 1) The zones are FIXED offsets, by design and stated in the picker's own comment - Skotiq carries no IANA database, so a site that observes DST is on standard time all year. The legacy migration maps to standard time deliberately rather than guessing a summer rule. 2) imaging_service.dart:336 exposureStartedAt is corrected by the same contract change but has no dedicated test: it is only READ on the timed-out-exposure branch, which needs exposureTime + 30 s of real time to reach, so a test for it would add ~31 s to the unit suite. Its consequence is real - with a positive site offset the stale-frame check rejected every frame a timed-out exposure returned, with a negative one it stopped firing at all - and it is a one-token change of the same idiom the tested sites use. 3) Deliberately NOT changed, because now() there is the display semantic and switching it would relocate the bug: cockpit_standby.dart's date, location_settings' own 'now HH:MM' subtitle, SessionExportService's 'exported at' header, session_provider's SessionService nowProvider (used only for in-memory checkpoint deltas that are self-consistent), and project_tracking_panel's 30-day rolling cutoff. 4) Not re-driven on a live GUI; the verifier's original repro was a running app on display :85.
still_open: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/dashboard/widgets/cockpit_recent_frames.dart:293 _timeLabel() renders a frame's capturedAt with .toLocal(), i.e. host-local, in the recent-frames tooltip. Same class, but it is a per-frame provenance label rather than a night-planning clock face, and the underlying instant is now correct - listing it rather than widening this change further.

The ~40 other HH:MM renderings outside the Dashboard/status-bar/planetarium set (sequencer run dashboard, analytics night-story timeline, planner queue) still print host-local. They were out of the finding's scope and several of them are session-forensics timestamps where host-local is arguably right; a deliberate product decision about which surfaces are 'observatory time' would settle them as a group.
